children: Suspension from Permanent Labour Certification Tanya Pandey & Surabhi Agarwal New Delhi: The four Indian IT services companies suspended by the United States Labour Department from the employment-based green card process-Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech-together recorded just 61 certified Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) filings in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 (Oct 1, 2025-June 30, 2026), with HCL America recording 59 certified cases and TCS only two.

Infosys and Wipro had no recorded cases in the period and neither did US-headquartered Cognizant. In the previous fiscal year, the number for the top Indian IT companies was 1,429. An ET analysis of US Department of Labour data shows that while American technology companies are bigger users of the programme, which allows foreign workers on H-1B visas to apply for permanent residency or the green card, employers in non-tech sectors such as food, meat and seafood were among the programme's biggest users.

TCS CEO K Krithivasan told ET on Friday that the suspension would have no impact on the company's business model or delivery of client projects, noting that its applications to convert H-1B visa holders to green-card holders had been in the single digits annually over the past two years. "We have close to 40,000 people in the US, and more than 50% of them are permanent residents or citizens," he said, adding that TCS files such applications occasionally when clients want the company to retain an employee for the long term. Foreign workers can stay in the US on an H-1B visa for six years, after which they have to return or apply for a green card. Consider the data for fiscal 2025. Of the 15 largest filers that year, five were technology companies and 10 were non-tech employers.

title: US Green Card Curbs may have Little Impact on Indian IT Cos
